At each node test thresholds between adjacent distinct feature values. Choose the largest reduction in weighted Gini impurity, then recurse subject to depth and minimum-leaf constraints. Leaves predict the majority class with deterministic ties. This reference is deliberately exhaustive and supports finite continuous features; missing-value routing, categorical splits, pruning, and histogram acceleration are separate extensions.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** A node's Gini impurity is $1-\sum_cp_c^2$. Split gain subtracts the child impurities weighted by their fractions of parent examples. Test only boundaries between distinct sorted values, enforce minimum leaf size before accepting a split, and separate split selection from stopping rules to make tie behavior reproducible.
